h: Pargeting, ship burials and a Suffolk bounce
p: Inflatable parks are at their best when everyone's dressed for the job. Leggings or joggers and long-sleeved tops make the slides much more comfortable, and long hair tied back stops it getting in the way on the climbing sections. If you're bringing a party, agree on a plan for drinks and food afterwards so the excitement doesn't turn into a hungry meltdown on the way home.

Ipswich has a few gems worth combining with a bounce. In the town centre, the Ancient House on the Buttermarket is a timber-framed building famous for its decorative pargeting, the raised plasterwork on its walls, and it's a lovely thing to stop and look at. Football fans will know Portman Road, home of Ipswich Town, which sits close to the centre.

A bit further out, Sutton Hoo near Woodbridge is a National Trust site where the famous Anglo-Saxon ship burial was discovered, and the viewing tower, exhibitions and walking trails make a great family outing. Jimmy's Farm, south of the town near Wherstead, has animals, a nature trail and farm shop. If you fancy the seaside, Felixstowe is a short drive away with a long promenade, beach huts and views of the huge container ships coming in. As you drive across the Orwell Bridge, keep an eye out for the river stretching away below, it's quite a sight. Back in town, the waterfront is a nice place to finish with an ice cream, watching the boats come and go from the marina while the kids recount every slide and tumble. Christchurch Park is also free and only a short walk from the centre, if anybody still has the legs for a play.
